title: Regulated workloads landing page design (wireframes → hi-fi) for ABM pilot
creator: Ben Carter
description:
Goal: Design a regulated workloads landing page to support the 6–8 week Vertical ABM pilot (initially finserv + healthcare). The page must be credible for security/compliance-driven buyers, map clearly to Redwood Dedicated + Redwood Private, and convert to the right next step (security review call / architecture consult / pilot).

Primary audiences:
- Security / GRC (CISO, Security Engineering, Compliance): wants clear controls, auditability, and “no surprises” language.
- Platform / ML Engineering: wants deployment topology, performance, reliability, and integration details.
- Procurement / Vendor mgmt: wants packaging clarity and evidence request path.

Design requirements:
- Reuse Redwood marketing components where possible (hero, feature cards, accordion FAQ, CTA banner, two-column section layouts) to keep implementation fast and consistent.
- Support two adjacent narratives without building two separate pages: (1) Dedicated for predictable throughput + isolation, (2) Private (VPC/on‑prem) for regulated / restricted networking.
- Ensure compliance-safe language and visual hierarchy that makes “what we do / what we don’t claim” obvious.
- Accessibility: meet WCAG 2.1 AA for typography, contrast, focus states, and motion.

Success criteria:
- First scroll answers: “Can you deploy in my environment?”, “How do you handle auditability, encryption, retention?”, “What’s the next step?”
- Clear CTA and secondary CTAs (Evidence Pack request, Security FAQ, Pilot plan).
- Page structure is modular for future vertical variants (finserv / healthcare sections can be swapped or expanded without redesign).
scope_notes:
In scope:
- Wireframes + hi-fi comps (desktop + mobile), including section-level annotations for engineering/docs implementation.
- Component selection + reuse plan for Redwood web system.
- Accessibility review checklist + design fixes.
- 1–2 iteration loops based on PMM + Security feedback.

Out of scope:
- New net-new design system components (avoid custom interactions).
- Complex interactive calculators or multi-step forms.
- Claim substantiation work (content owner: PMM + Security).
wireframe_structure:
Proposed page outline (v2):
1) Hero: “Production LLM inference for regulated workloads” + subhead emphasizing deployment flexibility (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) + short trust line (SOC2/ISO references only if approved in copy)
2) Problem framing: latency/cost/reliability under compliance constraints
3) Deployment options module:
   - Dedicated: reserved capacity, isolation, predictable throughput
   - Private: VPC/on-prem, customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integrations (as approved), audit logs
   - “How to choose” mini-table (Dedicated vs Private)
4) Security + compliance controls (icon list): encryption, audit logging, RBAC/SSO/SAML, retention/residency (careful wording), incident response path
5) Reference architecture (static diagram): request flow + control plane boundaries; include callouts for log export and key management boundary
6) Operational tooling (Console): token-level cost/latency breakdown, rollouts, fallback policies (tie back to reliability)
7) Pilot plan section (3 steps): discovery → benchmark → security review → pilot kickoff (keep generic)
8) FAQs (accordion): “Do you train on my data?”, “How do evidence requests work?”, “Where do logs live?”, “Can I run on-prem?”
9) CTA banner: “Book a security + architecture review” + secondary: “Request evidence pack index”
component_reuse_plan:
Reuse components (preferred):
- Standard marketing hero (H1 + subhead + 1 primary CTA + 1 secondary link)
- Feature card grid (3–6 cards) for controls + differentiators
- Two-column “image + text” blocks for architecture + Console screenshots
- Accordion for security FAQ
- Simple comparison table (existing table styles)
- Sticky anchor nav (optional; only if already supported in site templates)

Avoid:
- Custom tabs (unless already available) for Dedicated vs Private; prefer stacked modules with clear headings for accessibility.
- Autoplay video; if demo video is included, must be click-to-play with captions and transcript link.
accessibility_notes:
Accessibility checklist (design):
- Color contrast: verify all text over backgrounds meets WCAG AA (especially muted gray labels and button states).
- Typography: minimum body 16px, line height ≥ 1.4; avoid all-caps for long labels.
- Focus states: ensure visible focus ring on CTAs, accordion toggles, and any in-page anchor links.
- Motion: no essential info conveyed only by animation; respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- Images/diagrams: provide alt text guidance and ensure diagram is readable on mobile (consider simplified mobile variant or stacked callouts).
- Forms (if any): explicit labels (not placeholder-only), clear error messaging, and keyboard navigable.
content_and_claims_guardrails:
Guardrails from PMM/Security review (reflected in layout + annotation):
- Avoid “HIPAA-certified” / “HIPAA compliant” claims on the page. Use “supports HIPAA-adjacent workflows” only if PMM/Security approve final wording.
- Keep SOC2/ISO language factual and scoped; if referenced, link to the Security FAQ / evidence process rather than making broad assurances.
- Data retention/residency: avoid absolute statements unless explicitly supported by the product + contract terms; phrase as configurable / customer-controlled where accurate.
- Keep “on‑prem” language as an option with scoping (regulated/air-gapped package) and route to a consult CTA.
iteration_log:
2025-05-06 (Wireframes v1): Delivered initial layout with Dedicated vs Private as stacked modules; CTA = “Book a security review call”.
2025-05-09 (Review w/ Soojin + Naomi): Requested clearer separation between “security controls” and “deployment boundary”; remove any implied certification language; add evidence pack request path.
2025-05-13 (Hi-fi v1): Added reference architecture diagram block and a short “How evidence requests work” section; updated CTA hierarchy to include Evidence Pack Index as secondary.
2025-05-16 (Hi-fi v2 + a11y pass): Increased contrast on secondary text + link styles; standardized spacing to match existing marketing template; changed accordion hit targets for mobile.
2025-05-20 (Handoff): Final annotations sent to Docs/Eng for PR-421 implementation; provided mobile comp + exportables.
handoff_notes:
Handoff package includes:
- Desktop comp (1440) + mobile comp (390)
- Section-by-section annotations (intended semantics: H2/H3 order, list vs paragraph, table markup)
- Asset exports (SVG icons, architecture diagram as SVG + PNG fallback)
- Screenshot placeholders (Console: latency/cost breakdown; routing/fallback screen) with guidance on redaction

Implementation notes:
- Prefer static assets + lazy-load below the fold.
- Keep primary CTA consistent with ABM tracking (UTM-safe links).
open_questions:
Resolved:
- CTA: primary = “Book a security + architecture review”, secondary = “Request evidence pack index”.
- Dedicated vs Private: no tabs; stacked modules with mini comparison table.

Deferred / follow-ups:
- Confirm whether sticky anchor nav is supported in the chosen docs/marketing template; if not, ship without.
- Confirm final copy for data retention/residency lines after Legal wording is finalized.
